subject.title: [Bug]: cron.remove does not clean up session records in sessions.json

question: Should deleted cron jobs purge their base session rows immediately during `cron.remove`, or should orphaned base rows be removed only through guarded retention cleanup?
rationale: Current main leaves the rows, related PR work shows live base rows can preserve model/auth/label choices, and the open candidate fixes use different cleanup timing and ownership boundaries.

options.title: Split Cleanup Scopes
options.body: Land or revise guarded retention cleanup for stale orphan base rows, then keep this issue or a follow-up focused on immediate delete-time UI cleanup if delayed cleanup is not acceptable.

options.title: Immediate Delete Cleanup
options.body: Make `cron.remove` purge the deleted job's base and run session rows with tests for active-run, per-agent, and transcript behavior.

options.title: Retention-Only Cleanup
options.body: Treat deleted-job session rows as retention-managed state and close this issue only after maintainers accept that delayed cleanup satisfies the reported UI problem.

recommendation.title: Split Cleanup Scopes
recommendation.body: Land or revise guarded retention cleanup for stale orphan base rows, then keep this issue or a follow-up focused on immediate delete-time UI cleanup if delayed cleanup is not acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: openperf owns the active member PR currently shaping the guarded cron base-session cleanup semantics maintainers need to accept or revise.
